chunks: 2. Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isam al-Kulayni, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Ya`qub al-Kulayni said: Ahmad ibn Idris on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa on the authority of `Ali ibn Sayf on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Ubaydah that I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him)

about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High, to Iblis: (What prevented you that you should do obeisance to him whom I created with My Two Hands? Are you proud or are you of the exalted ones?)? He (AS) replied: “It means `With My Omnipotence and My Power.’” The Compiler of this book says: I have heard one of the Shi`ite scholars in Naysabur mentioning that Imams (peace be upon them) used to stop at these Word of Allah when mentioning this verse: What prevented you that you should do obeisance to him whom I created. Then they would continue with Word of the Mighty and High: “With My Two Hands, are you proud or are you of the exalted ones?” He also said: It is like the statement of a person: “With my sword you are fighting with me, and with my spear you are attacking me.” It is as if the Mighty and High is saying that “My Bounties have strengthened your pride and insubordination.”
What prevented you that you should do obeisance to him whom I created with My Two Hands? Are you proud or are you of the exalted ones?
With my sword you are fighting with me, and with my spear you are attacking me.
My Bounties have strengthened your pride and insubordination.
ai.seo_question: What does 'created with My Two Hands' mean in the context of Iblis?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tawhid elucidates the phrase 'created with My Two Hands' as a metaphor for divine power and favor rather than physical limbs, aligning with the Shia doctrine of divine simplicity. The Imam highlights a rhetorical pause after 'whom I created' to emphasize that it was God's bestowed grace (ni'mah) that empowered Iblis, enabling his subsequent pride and disobedience.
